newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says Trucks back on track '97.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says Trucks back on track '97.

text.p: Swedish automotive group AB Volvo said on Wednesday its truck unit would achieve healthy profitability in North America in 1998.

"We'll achieve healthy profitability in North America in 1998. We'll reach break-even in the first half of 1997. The programme is set," Volvo Truck President Karl-Erling Trogen told a news conference.

Trogen said Volvo's new VN Truck series had been well received in the United States, and that the company had taken 1,500 orders for the trucks to date. The first production models would be delivered soon, he said.
"With the VN series and the efforts we are now making we are sure of success in North America. We have great confidence in this," Trogen said.
Among these efforts are the closure of one factory, the setting up of a new customer financing faclity and improved after market and retailer services.
"North America is a distinct business opportunity for us," Trogen said.
"Our presence there has a positive effect on all of our operations. We will succeed despite a tougher business climate where we expect the total market to fall to around 180,000 trucks in 1997."
